theorems.statement: For arbitrary finite explicit positive-rational recurrent branch systems, the powered critical potentials on critical SCCs extend to a global positive rational potential H with powered ratio lambda_e=1 exactly for critical dominant branches and 0<lambda_e<1 for every other explicit branch. A constructive quotient-cycle slack and maximum-simple-path potential gives such H. Any chosen H yields an exact full finite exponential moment jet with dominant layer K.
theorems.reducible_boundary: When several critical equality classes remain, independent class multipliers change individual inter-class lambda_e. Closed excursion products and grouped characteristic cycle-system ratios are invariant; the reducible full branch-ratio jet is a gauge representative rather than a canonical per-edge coordinate system.

theorems.statement: For any global strict powered gauge the exact characteristic polynomial has a finite gauge-invariant expansion P_s(z)=p_K(z)+sum_{eta<1} eta^s G_eta(z), because determinant exponential bases are closed ratio products. If the selected smallest positive root z_* of p_K is simple, strict layers are exactly classifiable as root-active or root-inactive by G_eta(z_*). If all strict layers are inactive the Perron root is unchanged; otherwise the largest root-active eta_* gives ln rho_s=ln rho_*+[G_eta*(z_*)/(z_*p_K'(z_*))] eta_*^s+o(eta_*^s), with positive Perron coefficient.
theorems.semantics: Feed-forward strict branches can be root-inactive, while closed excursions through losing critical/noncritical blocks can be root-active. This is the reducible simple-root replacement for irreducible max-branch-ratio gap selection.

theorems.statement: If the selected smallest positive root z_* of p_K has multiplicity r>=2, each strict characteristic layer has contact order q_eta=ord_{z_*}G_eta. For q_eta<r its candidate first root scale is the exact radical state theta_eta^(r-q_eta)=eta. Candidate scales compare by rational integer powers. The maximal candidate scale theta_* determines the first Newton edge; after z=z_*+theta_*^s y, the scaled characteristic polynomial tends to E(y)=a_r y^r+sum_{theta_eta=theta_*} b_eta y^q_eta. If the Perron-selected negative edge root y_* is simple, z_s=z_*+y_*theta_*^s+o(theta_*^s) and ln rho_s=ln rho(K)-(y_*/z_*)theta_*^s+o(theta_*^s).
theorems.boundary: A multiple selected edge root requires a later Newton edge. Determinant-base ordering can differ from root-scale ordering because contact order changes the exponent denominator.

negative_boundaries.statement: Independent critical-class rescaling changes individual inter-class powered branch ratios in reducible systems. Only closed ratio products/characteristic layers are canonical gauge invariants.

In reducible systems the largest strict branch ratio can be feed-forward/root-inactive. With multiple selected roots, even the largest determinant base need not give the largest root scale because contact orders alter the Newton exponent.
The simple-root response formula G(z_*)/(z_*p_K'(z_*)) is invalid when p_K'(z_*)=0. Tied critical classes can produce fractional Puiseux exponents such as (ab)^(s/2).
WBRC-T51 selects and validates only the first Newton edge. If the selected edge root is multiple or further coefficients are required, later Newton edges are a separate research task.

The addendum is finite-state, explicit positive-rational and unsigned. It does not promote signed/amplitude cancellation, complex or arbitrary irrational branch weights, infinite-state recurrence, a floating eigensolver, or a general symbolic Puiseux-series engine.
